title: Ring Gap Structure around Class I Protostar WL 17
question: Does the Class I protostar WL 17 have a ring-hole or a ring-gap structure, is an outflow associated with it, and what do these imply for ring formation timescale and planet formation?

data.sensitivity: 18 uJy/beam continuum (high-res); 0.33 mJy/beam continuum and 0.35 K per 0.1 km/s for CO lines (low-res)

what.value: ALMA Band 3 ring-hole results (hole radius ~10-13 au, outer ring ~20 au, 0.06''x0.05'' beam, 36 uJy/beam)

evidence.quote: They found that WL 17 has a ring–hole structure based on high angular resolution ALMA Band 3 observations, where the radius of the hole is $\sim10$ au and the outer radius of the ring is $\sim20$ au.

what.value: Single-dish 12CO(3-2) outflow properties (lengths, masses, velocities, t_dyn, rate) and v_sys = 4 km/s

evidence.quote: We determined the outflow maximum velocity $v_{\rm max}$ with the system velocity $v_{\rm sys}=$ 4 km s$^{-1}$ (cite: van_der_Marel_2013).

what.value: Inner disk radii, fluxes and ring radii of ring-gap protoplanetary disks for comparison

evidence.quote: We compare the properties of the inner disk of the WL 17 system with those of other inner disks of objects associated with the ring–gap structure presented in (cite: Francis_2020).

what.value: Spectral index alpha=2 assumed for converting sensitivity to 3 mm
Herschel column density map of the region

evidence.loc: 4.1 Remaining Mass of Core and Envelope around WL 17
evidence.quote: Figure [9](#fig:herschel) shows the column density map derived from the Herschel Gould Belt Survey data (cite: Andre_2010)

recipe.method: tclean with Briggs weighting; imcontsub for lines

recipe.goal: Fit ring geometry and radial profile
recipe.method: Peak radius every 1 deg in polar coordinates fitted with an ellipse; deproject; azimuthally average; Gaussian fits to inner disk and outer ring peaks

recipe.goal: Dust and gas mass of ring/disk
recipe.method: Optically thin M_dust = F d^2 /(kappa B(T)) on flux above 5 sigma
assumptions: kappa=2 cm2/g, T_dust=20 K, gas-to-dust 100, d=137 pc

recipe.goal: Outflow velocity, timescale, mass, mass-loss rate
recipe.method: PV diagrams give v_max; t_dyn = r_out/v_max tan(i); M_out = mu m_H A N_ave with N = X_CO W_CO; Mdot = M_out/t_dyn
key_parameters: Outflow area: intensity > 0.5 K km/s; v_sys = 4 km/s; i_out = i_ring
assumptions: mu = 2.8; X_CO = 2.0e20; protostellar mass 1 Msun for Keplerian; constant mass loss rate

recipe.goal: Envelope mass from C18O and Herschel
recipe.method: Optical depth from T_B (Tex = 10, 20 K), column density, convert to H2 and mass over area; Herschel mass within 1000, 2000, 3000 au minus background 1.5e22 cm-2
key_parameters: T_B ~1.1 K; Delta v ~0.8 km/s from Gaussian fit; nu = 220 GHz

recipe.method: t_grow = M_disk/Mdot_acc with Mdot_acc = epsilon Mdot_out

answer_key.quantity: Ring inner and outer edge radii

evidence.quote: the inner and outer edge radius of the outer ring are 11 and 21 au, respectively
the estimated FWHM ($5.2$ au) as the upper limit of the radius
we estimated an inclination angle $i_{\rm ring}$ of 33.8$^{\circ}$ and a PA of 68.7$^{\circ}$
the peak radius of the outer ring is 15.7 au and the FWHM is 8.8 au
The total flux is $F_{\nu} = 4.37 \times$10$^{-2}$ Jy, which is the sum of the inner disk (6.6$\times$10$^{-4}$ Jy) and outer ring (4.3$\times$10$^{-2}$ Jy).
The total dust mass was estimated to be $M_{\rm dust}$=7.4$\times$10$^{-5}\,M_{\odot}$.
The total mass of the blue-shifted and red-shifted outflows is $M_{\rm out,total}=$8.7$\times$10$^{-4}\, M_{\odot}$
we estimated the total mass loss rate (sum of the red and blue shifted outflows) of 3.6$\times$10$^{-7}$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$

evidence.loc: 4.1 Remaining Mass of Core and Envelope around WL 17
evidence.quote: The mass of molecular hydrogen estimated from C$^{18}$O is $4\times10^{-3}\,{M}_\odot$.
H$_2$ & Black circle (c) in Fig. [9](#fig:herschel), $R < 3000$ au & 0.9$^\ast$ & 2.8 & 1.1$\times$10$^{-1}$
the disk growth timescale is as short as $(M_{\rm disk}/\dot{M}_{\rm acc}) \sim 10^4$ yr

score_reason: Public data and a clear recipe for the main numbers, but imaging details, regions and several assumptions are not fully stated.
